title: embeddings-rerank-debug-scratch
content:
Summary:
- Working notes for the embeddings + rerank endpoint anomalies observed 2025-02-14 -> 2025-02-15. Two related symptoms: (A) dimension mismatch errors surfaced in downstream reranker that expects 1536-d vectors but sometimes receives 1024-d vectors, (B) intermittent latency spikes for the rerank endpoint (p95 increased from ~120ms to 600-900ms during some windows).

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-14 02:50 UTC: Canary rollout of embedding model variant `embed-open-quant-v2` started (auto-rollout policy).
- 2025-02-14 03:12 UTC: Pager alert for high error rate on rerank route (customer-facing).
- 2025-02-14 03:18 UTC: First dimension-mismatch logs appear in rerank service: "ValueError: expected 1536 but got 1024".
- 2025-02-14 03:40 UTC: Reverted embed model rollout to `embed-open-v1` (rollback).
- 2025-02-14 04:05 UTC: Error rate reduced but p95 latency still elevated in some buckets.
- 2025-02-15 ongoing: Investigating root cause, trying reproductions locally and in staging.

Errors / log snippets collected:
- reranker logs:
  [2025-02-14T03:17:20Z] ERROR rerank-service: failed to process request id=abc123: VectorDimensionMismatch: expected=1536 got=1024 source=embeddings-service
  [2025-02-14T03:17:20Z] DEBUG rerank-service: received vector len=1024 model=embed-open-quant-v2

- embeddings service logs:
  [2025-02-14T03:15:03Z] WARN embeddings: model selected embed-open-quant-v2 (quantized) instance=runner-5
  [2025-02-14T03:15:03Z] INFO model-runner: returned embedding vector length=1024 for model embed-open-quant-v2 request_id=abc123

- network/ingress logs (no obvious 5xx spikes except time-aligned p95 increases):
  p95 timeline (example bucket): 02:30 -> 120ms, 03:00 -> 150ms, 03:12 -> 650ms, 03:30 -> 700ms, 04:00 -> 240ms

Commands and repro attempts (local/staging):
1) Quick curl to embeddings endpoint used in prod routing (staging):
   curl -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"embed-open-quant-v2","input":"test sentence"}'
   -> returns vector length 1024 (confirm)

2) Pin to non-quantized model:
   curl -d '{"model":"embed-open-v1","input":"test sentence"}' ...
   -> returns vector length 1536 (expected)

3) Python snippet used to compare shapes across batch sizes in staging:
   from requests import post
   for s in [1,4,8,16]:
       r = post(url, json={"model":"embed-open-quant-v2","input":["x"]*s}, headers=headers).json()
       print(s, len(r['data'][0]['embedding']))
   -> consistently 1024 for quant variant across batch sizes

4) Reproduction of latency spikes with synthetic traffic:
   - Ran k6 load against rerank route with mixture of real-size queries and 40% rerank calls. Observed p95 jump when routing started selecting runners with quant-variant (same time correlation).

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: The quantized model variant (`embed-open-quant-v2`) intentionally produces 1024-d vectors (a model change) but routing rules did not update downstream consumers who expect 1536. Canary rollout propagated quant variant to some customers -> dimension mismatch.
- H2: Model runner automatically applies a dimensionality reduction post-processing step for quant models (bug introduced) reducing vector length unexpectedly.
- H3: Smart routing/fallback picked a different embedding model (compatible function but different dim) due to capacity constraints; mismatch between model catalog metadata and runtime selection.
- H4: Latency spikes caused by kernel selection path for quant model on specific GPU types (gpu pool with older drivers), causing slower execution/p99 due to fallbacks to CPU or degraded batching.
- H5: KV prefix caching disabled during the rollout (config change), increasing upstream load on reranker and causing p95 latency to spike.

Quick checks/results so far:
- Confirmed quant variant returns 1024-d in staging (curl + python).
- Model catalog entry in productdb for embed-open-quant-v2 incorrectly set dims=1536 (metadata mismatch) -> this is big.
- GitHub PR referenced in linked_artifacts contains runtime changes that added a new inference path for quant models; TODO: review lines that alter postprocess/embedding shape.
- Checked deployment hosts for runner-5: CUDA driver version differs from fleet default on one host; need to compare perf traces.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rolled back canary for embed-open-quant-v2 (2025-02-14 03:40 UTC).
- Added a temporary validation in rerank-service: if len(vec) != expected_dim -> return 422 and log more metadata (customer impact reduced).
- Pin critical customers to embed-open-v1 and set routing policy to require exact-dim compatibility.

Next action items (owners):
- Maya: review model-runner PR #983 for any postprocess/shape-change code paths (in progress).
- Evan: update productdb catalog entry for embed-open-quant-v2 dims -> set to 1024 OR change model artifact to produce 1536; coordinate with model team. (owner: Evan Zhao)
- Ravi: run perf traces on runner-5 host and compare kernel selection timeline vs runner-1 (owner: Ravi Singh).
- Platform: add a pre-deploy validation to ensure model metadata dims == runtime output dims (ticket created JIRA-INC-4821).
- SRE: investigate if KV caching flags were toggled during rollout window (quick check).

Notes to self / rough hypotheses to test next:
- Re-run embeddings with explicit postprocess disabled to see if shape changes (maybe a config toggle introduced in runtime PR).
- Try forcing quant runner on a node with same driver as baseline to separate driver vs quant path perf issues.
- Add unit test in rerank-service that fails fast if embedding dims != expected; long-term, support runtime-registered compatibility map for models.

Rough timeline for fix:
- Short term (hours): keep rollback + customer pins, patch rerank validation, update catalog to reflect actual dims.
- Mid term (days): revert problematic runtime change OR make embed runner produce expected dims, add CI check, update rollout gating.
- Long term: route-by-dim compatibility enforcement and stronger pre-deploy checks in productdb and model-runner CI.

Other references / notes:
- Customer-facing incident brief draft stored in drive: (TODO create link)
- Keep this doc as scratchpad; will distill into incident postmortem after root cause confirmed.

-- maya
